rosterSizingRule.decision: THIS RESOLVES C-032's parked finding E14, and it does so WITHOUT changing any committed code. The question was why handlePlanReview floors its roster at its lens set while handleVetTest sizes purely by readFanout. The coherent rule, which 9.5a must follow: FLOOR AT THE SET WHERE THE SPEC NAMES A COVERAGE SET; CLAMP TO readFanout WHERE THE SPEC NAMES ONLY A COUNT.
rosterSizingRule.why: A named coverage set is a correctness requirement — dropping a lens means a plan or an item 'passed review' on evidence nobody gathered. A bare count is a throughput knob, and clamping it costs nothing but wall-clock breadth.
application: planReview — §3.2 names FOUR lenses (a SET) -> floor. Matches committed 9.3 (Math.max(readFanout, PLAN_REVIEW_LENSES.length)); its recorded deviation is hereby JUSTIFIED rather than merely noted.

itemReview — §3.3 names FIVE MANDATORY lenses, explicitly 'never truncated by configuration' (a SET) -> floor, expressed through the clamp(.,3,6) + pairwise-merge rule so that three sessions still cover five lenses.
vet — §3.3 says 'vetCritics parallel critics': a COUNT with no named set -> clamp. Matches committed 9.4a; nothing to change.
skeptics — skepticsPerFinding is a COUNT -> clamp.
rosterSizingRule.consequence: parallel.maxReaders is a wall-clock concurrency ceiling the fan-out engine enforces internally; it is NEVER a coverage truncation. Report this resolution at the Phase 9 gate so E14 can be closed.

specGaps: GAP (session count vs maxReaders) — RESOLVED BY rosterSizingRule above: sessions = clamp(readFanout('itemReview', config), 3, 6), and the sub-3 warning fires whenever the PRE-clamp value is below 3, whichever knob caused it.

GAP (clamp-warning event name) — RESOLVED, no widening: emit a level:'warn' JournalRecord on the EXISTING fanout 'subsession.dispatched' event of the first review dispatch, with data naming the configured and clamped values. JournalRecord.level is committed (types.ts:435).

GAP (which lenses are 'quality'): §3.3 says a surviving spec/contract finding discards 'that round's quality-lens findings' but never lists them. RESOLUTION, from doctrine review.md's own tiering ('meets its requirement and behaves correctly' vs 'style, structure, polish'): the discard TRIGGER is a surviving spec/contract finding; the DISCARDED-and-re-derived set is test-adequacy, minimality/simplification and perf; correctness and guardrail are tier-1 and are RETAINED and fixed alongside the spec findings.

GAP (the 'where cheap' reverted-behaviour probe): §3.3 wants the changed test to 'still fail against a reverted-behavior probe where cheap' without defining cheap. RESOLUTION: attempt the probe iff the item's fileScope is non-empty and its working-tree changes round-trip via `git stash push -- <fileScope>` / `git stash pop`, restoring in a finally; ANY stash failure skips the probe. The probe AUGMENTS and never replaces the mandatory re-run + re-vet. One row pins the probe firing, one pins the skip path still re-running and re-vetting.

GAP (pushback detection): §3.3 says a wrong finding is 'answered with reasoning' and gets one more skeptic round, but no schema field carries the pushback. RESOLUTION, no widening: pushback = a fix dispatch returning ImplementerResult status 'DONE_WITH_CONCERNS' whose concerns[] names the finding id. NEEDS_CONTEXT and BLOCKED follow the standard implementer-status escalation instead.

GAP (under-delivered panel: which branch): the binding allows EITHER re-dispatching the missing skeptics OR counting them as UPHOLDS. RESOLUTION for determinism: exactly ONE re-dispatch attempt of the missing sessions, then any verdict still missing counts as UPHOLD (conservative — keep the finding). The assertion row accepts either observable outcome so the binding's letter is preserved; this pin is for the implementer.

assertions.text: with workflow.itemReviewers 3, conductor_item_review dispatches EXACTLY three fresh reviewer sub-sessions (role 'reviewer', schema Findings) in the §3.3 merged composition — spec/contract+correctness, guardrail+minimality, test-adequacy+perf — so ALL FIVE mandatory lenses still dispatch; asserted on the fake's recorded prompts: three pairwise-different prompts each naming its own lens pair, every dispatch carrying the item's diff + spec + test

the §3.3 session-count rule holds at the other configs: 6 dispatches six sessions one lens each, ADDING perf; 5 merges minimality+perf; 4 additionally merges test-adequacy into spec/contract; below 3 clamps to 3 and journals a warn-level record on an existing closed-vocabulary event; merging NEVER drops a mandatory lens at any count. Per rosterSizingRule, a parallel.maxReaders below the floor must NOT truncate the lens set
a run flagged trivial uses the trivial merged composition even when itemReviewers is 6, and the guardrail lens provably survives the merge — no trivial-mode compression removes a mandatory lens

a round in which a spec/contract finding SURVIVES its skeptics discards that round's quality-lens findings (test-adequacy, minimality, perf): they are routed to NO fix dispatch, and after the spec fix and its re-validate a FRESH quality derivation is dispatched before any quality finding is acted on — asserted on the fake's dispatch sequence. Correctness and guardrail findings are tier-1 and are NOT discarded

every finding gets exactly workflow.skepticsPerFinding skeptic sub-sessions (schema Verdict) and survival is decided by core/verdict findingSurvives, never reimplemented: with k=2 a one-uphold/one-overturn TIE UPHOLDS the finding; a REFUTED finding triggers no fix dispatch, no re-validate, and contributes nothing at the round cap

MANDATORY DEFERRED BINDING (Phase 1 gate, verdict.findingSurvives): with skepticsPerFinding 2, one skeptic env-failed and the sole returned verdict an OVERTURN, the handler must NOT feed the partial panel straight to findingSurvives — which would read the missing verdict as an overturn and DROP the finding. It either re-dispatches the missing skeptic or counts the missing verdict as UPHOLD; asserted outcome: the finding SURVIVES. A real major is never dropped because a skeptic session crashed

routing by path (§3.3 table row 1): a surviving finding whose fix touches ONLY the item's fileScope dispatches an implementer, and the fix is followed by re-validate then re-review — asserted on the fake's dispatch order

routing by path (§3.3 table row 2): a test-adequacy finding — and any finding whose suggestedFix names a testScope path — dispatches a TEST-WRITER and NEVER the implementer (zero implementer dispatches for it: the implementer is gated to fileScope and would hit a guaranteed edit-gate denial, burning review rounds on a mandatory lens). The changed test RE-ENTERS the test discipline: it is re-run through evidence and re-vetted with vetCritics critics BEFORE re-validate and re-review

routing by path (§3.3 table row 3): a surviving finding whose fix touches BOTH scopes dispatches the testWriter FIRST and the implementer SECOND, sequentially, each under its own discipline, before re-validate and re-review

the 'where cheap' probe, both branches: when the item's fileScope changes round-trip through git stash, the changed test is proven to STILL FAIL against the reverted tree (so it pins behaviour rather than the implementation's shape) and the tree is restored in a finally; when the stash fails, the probe is SKIPPED and the mandatory re-run + re-vet still happen — the probe augments the discipline and never replaces it

an implementer that answers a routed finding with reasoning instead of implementing it (DONE_WITH_CONCERNS naming the finding id) is routed through exactly ONE extra skeptic round carrying that reasoning: a refuted finding then dies with no further fix demand, an upheld finding still requires the fix. Pushback is never accepted silently and never loops more than the one extra round

MANDATORY DEFERRED BINDING (Phase 8 gate / C-028): the fix-round dispatch that sends surviving findings to the implementer threads the 'receiving-review' signal so buildSystemAppend appends receive-review.md as a SECONDARY pack (tdd.md stays primary), mirroring the committed debug.md path — asserted on the DELIVERED system append for that implementer session, never on pack loading. Loaded is not delivered: that was the whole C-028 finding

a round with ZERO surviving findings advances VALIDATED->REVIEWED through legalItemTransition (never a direct state write), and a call against an item not at VALIDATED is refused by the same legality check BEFORE any dispatch

when workflow.reviewMaxRounds is exhausted with findings still surviving, the handler appends ONE §2.11 question with origin exactly 'review-round-cap' carrying the surviving finding list, and blocks the item via store.setBlocked — asserted by READING THE PERSISTED ITEM FILE back, never by inspecting a journal line
